title: Angle Bisector — Worked Example (a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ method)
topicTitle: Straight line: length of perpendicular from a given point to a given line, bisectors of the angles between two straight lines
summary: Angle Bisector — Worked Example (a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ method) covers essential principles and applications. Angle Bisector Between Two Lines — The a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ Rule covers essential principles and applications.
notes: **Bisector equations.** The angle bisectors of the lines a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 are (a₁x + b₁y + c₁)/√(a₁² + b₁²) = ± (a₂x + b₂y + c₂)/√(a₂² + b₂²).
**Equal distance property.** Any point on a bisector is equidistant from the two lines, using the perpendicular distance |ax + by + c|/√(a² + b²).
**Acute vs obtuse.** The two bisectors are perpendicular; when a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ < 0 the '+' combination bisects the acute angle, and when a₁a₂ + b₁b₂ > 0 it bisects the obtuse angle.
**Worked steps.** Write both equations in general form, divide each by the square root of the sum of its squared coefficients, combine with ±, and simplify each result.
**Use of the result.** The bisector equations locate the in-centre of a triangle (intersection of internal bisectors) and solve locus problems requiring equal distance from two lines.
